Bezantur, also known as the City of a Thousand Temples, and the Citadel of Thieves, was a foreboding but prosperous port city located at the southern coast of the Thayan tharch of Priador. It was as diverse a place that could be found in the nation, a religious hub for those oppressed by the centuries-long rule of the Red Wizards and their strict adherence to the worship of magic above all else.[2][3]

Though it lacked the joy and hope offered by the great metropolises of western Faerûn, it was the heart and soul of Thay, famous for its great harbor that opened up into the Alamber Sea.[4][3]

Description[]

Bezantur was enclosed within massive, black walls that loomed over its outer streets. The slums of Bezantur stuck to these walls and spread beyond their protection, in a grouping of shacks and inter-connected shanties known as Market Town.[5] The stench of the unwashed masses combined with burning refuse, roaming livestock and open sewer grates permeated this area and wafted well into the city proper.[3]

The famed harbor of Bezantur was nearly always packed to the brim with ships unloading their goods in and out of the city. Due to the lack of "official" taxes, Guild of Foreign Trade inspectors, along with their thieves' guild counterparts, were often found taking their cut of Bezanturan imports. While sharks, giant eels and octopuses inhabited the waters beneath the docks, sahuagin and even lacedons were known to come ashore and wreak havoc.[6] The harbor waters were known to be rich with wealth, thrown there as tributes to Umberlee by the inhabitants of the city. It was said that anyone fool enough to helm themselves to those riches would suffer death by drowning, regardless of how far they fled.[1]

Most of Bezantur's more reputable buildings, along with many of its temples, could be located in the heart of the city, at the end of the High Road just beyond the North Gate.[7] The southwest quarter was a labyrinthine maze warehouses, often used to arrange clandestine meetings and conduct illicit business,[3] while the northeast region, known as the Street of White Roses, was perhaps the most lawless part of the city known to some as the Citadel of Thieves.[8]

Law and Order[]

Crime was rampant throughout Bezantur. Mighty thieves' guilds conducted their operations without a care of repercussion from the authorities, thanks to their systematic bribery of Thayan officials. The gnolls and goblinoid creatures that served in the legions would regularly attack visitors in the open streets and were seldom thwarted by guards or constabulary.[3] The gang known as the White Ravens were known blackmailers and slave-traders.[9]

Economy[]

Bezantur was vital to the Thayan economy, as it controlled the majority of Thay sea trade across the Alamber Sea.[10] The neutral waters of the Alamber served as the primary route between Thay, Mulhorand, Unther,[11],Tymanther and High Imaskar.[12] Just about anything, or anyone, was available for purchase within the city.[3]

During the reign of tharchion Mari Agneh, taxes were completely eliminated in the city of Bezantur.[3]

The city housed the headquarters of the Guild of Foreign Trade, overseen by the ambitious and adept transmuter, Samas Kul,[13] who ascended to the rank of zulkir.[14]

Religion[]

Many different gods were worshiped in the great temples of Bezantur,[4] and it served as a religious center for the faithful whose worship was otherwise forgotten throughout Thay. Amongst the people of the city, the most popular deities were said to be Mask and Umberlee.[1]

Temples dedicated to the dark gods, such as Talos, Loviatar, Beshaba, the ancient Netherese deity Garagos,[15] and even the often-shunned Gargauth were prominent in Bezantur, along with those devoted to faiths that were long-forgotten following the Time of Troubles such as Bhaal and Leira. The non-human faithful of Thay were fairly well represented, as the city had sanctuaries devoted to the Orc pantheon, Juiblex, and even Lolth, the Dark Mother of the drow.[3]

Worship of the so-called "good" deities, like Chauntea, Sune and Mielikki, could be found in the city, though they were much harder to locate. Their respective clergies were regularly driven out of Bezantur by the followers of more-prominent faiths.[3]

While the city hosted major temples to Azuth and Mystra prior to the Time of Troubles,[16] open veneration of these gods was strictly forbidden following that event. The Red Wizards considered themselves guardians of the magic they hoarded, and abhorred any being, mortal or divine, who sought to disseminate the secrets of the Art.[3]

History[]

Bezantur was a city with over two millennia of history by the 14th century DR.[17] It was originally a bustling port city of Raumathar known as Kensten until it was taken over by the Red Wizards, renamed Bezantur, and established as its own tharch within the fledgling magocracy of Thay.[3]

Early Years[]

Kensten was founded by the Raumathar Empire for its location as a port on the Alamber Sea. It developed slowly due to its distance from the empire's core territories,[17] and remained a largely insignificant settlement.[18]

In the Year of Recompense, −150 DR, during the climax of the Great Conflagration between Raumathar and Narfell, Raumathari forces mustered at Kensten, prompting a attack by the Nar armies. In response, the Raumathari wizards summoned an avatar of the god Kossuth to defend the city. While the Lord of Flames did destroy the attackers, he then turned his attention to Kensten itself, burning the city and much of the surrounding coastline in retaliation for the Raumathari's audacity to summon him. Both armies were devastated and their respective empires irrevocably weakened, while the only survivors from Kensten were those who fled by boat to the island of Alaor.[17][18]

Kensten was later rebuilt and repopulated as a holding of Mulhorand in the Year of Old Beginnings, −135 DR. The Mulhorandi leaders erected a temple to Kossuth to appease the deity, despite the displeasure of their god-kings. The first high-priest of Kossuth in Kensten was named Bezantur.[17]

Thayan Conquest[]

When Thay gained independence from Mulhorand in the Year of the Spouting Fish, 922 DR, Kensten briefly became an independent city-state ruled by a mercantile council. However, it fell to the Red Wizards and was incorporated into Thay in the Year of Fireslaughter, 932 DR, after a fortnight-long siege. The invaders were aided by the treachery of Kossuth's priests—who resented the taxation imposed by the council—and the city was renamed to "Bezantur" in honor of the Kossuthan priest. By the Year of the Tightening Fist, 1074 DR, Bezantur had become its own tharch and was developing into Thay's mercantile and religious capital. The worship of Kossuth remained one of the city's dominant religious institutions, eventually becoming the de facto official religion within the City of a Thousand Temples.[17]

Following the Salamander War of the Year of the Prince, 1357 DR, the city was restructured as the capital of the newly-founded tharch of Priador. The previous tharchioness Mari Agneh competed with the ambitious evoker Aznar Thrul for leadership of the new province, but vanished under unknown circumstances. The newly-appointed zulkir Thrul, was awarded leadership over Priador, and made his home in Bezantur.[3]

Thayan Civil War[]

When undead forces ravaged the tharch of Pyarados, in Kythorn 1375 DR, the people of Bezantur celebrated with great fervor and cheered their apparent savior, the necromancer Szass Tam. It was one of the final insults to Aznar Thrul, that his political rival was celebrated for righting the calamity, which unbeknownst to Thrul, Tam had actually manufactured.[19]

In the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, the city of Bezantur was the setting for the final encounter between the legions of the Council of Zulkirs and those of the self-proclaimed regent Szass Tam during the Thayan civil war. The lich used the priests of Bane that were stationed in the town to force the zulkirs to flee aboard vessels to the islands of Alaor. The priests literally burned Bezantur's harbor to ashes in an attempt to destroy the zulkir's vessels as they fled. Szass then proclaimed the town's high priest of Bane, Zekidh Shezim, the new autharch of Bezantur.[20]

Notable Locations[]

Inns and Taverns
  • Myulon's Inn: Conveniently located near the North Gate on west side of the city, this inn offered quality accommodations to foreign visitors and was seldom harassed by city officials.[21]
  • Rusty Anchor: This dark and smokey inn featured its own barber and tattoo artist,[22] a practice that was popular to the point of prevalence among the mulan populace.[23]
  • Santhro's Rooming House: Rooms could be rented at the Temple of Garagos in the mid-to-late 14th century DR.[15]
  • Sea Wolf Inn: Despite the gnoll marauders that occasionally harassed its patrons, this inn offered fairly good food, even if the ale was a bit watered-down.[22]
  • Slain Sahuagin: A truly wretched establishment, this tavern had the distasteful reputation as the filthiest and least reputable location in Bezantur.[5] It was prone to regular flooding during particularly high tides.[22]
Landmarks
  • Central Cathedral: The black keep of Bezantur drew an imposing shadow over the city. Its housed most of the legion of Priador, over 4,000 humans, gnoll, goblins and other monstrous creatures. Within its upper levels were aviaries for the legion's darkenbeasts,[24] which were later used to stable the griffons of the Griffon Cavalry of Pyarados.[25]
  • Citadel of Correction: This imposing stone prison inspired fear in anyone who even thought about taking actions that may displease the red wizards. Within its dark halls were interrogation chambers, torture pits, and a maze-like dungeon that was believed to connect with the more horrifying depths of the Underdark.[8]
Residences
  • Canos estate: The wealthy and influential Canos family of Thay maintained a sprawling estate within the city.[24]
  • Narfel's rooming house: This run down, apartment complex
  • Serpent Tower: This slender, serpentine spire was home to Mythrellan,[note 1] the zulkir of illusion during the 14th century.[26][27]
Schools
  • Hexcidon: The only hexblade college in Faerûn served generations of warlocks as they studied to become elite bodyguards and generals in their service to Thay.[28]
Shops and Businesses
  • Caravansera: Mistress Nydra provided accommodations for the pack animals used by caravaneers that came to Bezantur from along the High Road.[21]
  • Mufrim's Place: This all-in-one business located in Market Town, served as an inn, tavern and general store.[21]
  • Nyrak's Second-hand Merchandise: This shop provided fencing services for the hard-pressed indigents of Bezantur's slums.[5]
  • Ruvya's Toys and Amusements: The joyful old toy-maker Ruvya spent most of his life within his workshop, crafting dolls, puppets, and intricate clockwork automatons for the children of Bezantur.[15]
Temples
  • Crypt of Imminent Death: A temple of Jergal, who was openly revered in Thay as death became a more prominent part of life throughout the nation's existence.[24][29]
  • Flaming Brazier: The sacred flames that burned within this grand temple of Kossuth did so with an intensity rivaled by the zeal of his Thayan faithful.[30][31][17]
  • House of Cyric: Converted from a massive temple-complex built to venerate Bhaal, this holy house of the Dark Sun was popular among the vast numbers of Cyricists in Bezantur.[32]
  • House of Entropy: The clergy in this mysterious sanctuary worshiped the banished primordial known as Entropy.[33][24]
  • House of Iyachtu Xvim: Xvimism was quite popular in Thay, and the Godson's faithful had a contentious relationship with the clergy of Cyric.[30]
  • Loviatar's Manor: Built into a small hillside in the center of the city, "The Manor" had a number of discreet chambers and public rooms where many Red Wizards, and even priests of other deities could enjoy the variety of services provided within.[24]
  • Orcish temple: The orc soldiers and guards serving within the Thayan legions were allowed to keep this crude holy house to worship their monstrous deities, demigods, and tribal heroes.[34]
  • Temple of Bane: Even in the years following his death, the Banite priests of the city maintained his temple and held vigil for his return to Toril.[8]
  • Temple of Beshaba: Lady Doom was largely venerated out of fear, as Thayan citizens wished to avoid the ill luck and poor fortune brought on by her clergy.[31]
  • Temple of Garagos: Run by the powerful and accomplished High Priest Santhro, this temple was one of the few holy houses of Garagos that remained in Faerûn as of the mid-14th century.[15]
  • Temple of Gargauth: Many depraved Thayans chose to revere the horrifying deity Gargauth despite the delight he took in feeding upon his own faithful.[21]
  • Temple of Leira: A small temple dedicated to the goddess of lies.[31]
  • Temple of Lolth: This temple was a grand, black dome adorned with silver spiderwebs. Above the main doorway was an inscription reading: "Lolth tlu malla; jal ultrinnan zhah xundus" (meaning in the Drow language: "Lolth be praised; all victory is her doing").[8]
  • Temple of Mask: The fortress-temple of Mask was overseen by Shabella the Pale, the guildmistress of the Bezanturan thieves' guild, who controlled all the illicit business that occurred in and around the city.[34][8]
  • Temple of Shar: Services held within this mysterious, dark temple were popular among the lower-class citizens and Red Wizards alike.[30]
  • Temple of Sharess: Established shortly before the year 1368 DR, this house of hedonism flourished in due part to the decadence sought by Bezantur's high-class citizens.[21]
  • Temple of Sune: The indulgent feasts and grand, extravagant festivals thrown by the Sunite priests drew many attendees from throughout Bezantur.[30]
  • Temple of Talona: One of the few places where the goddess of poison was worshiped openly, although this did not mean the people of Bezantur trusted the congregation.[32]
  • Temple of Talos: This square, granite sanctuary was one of the few permanent structures in all of Faerûn dedicated to the worship of Talos.[30]
  • Temple of Tempus: While the followers of Tempus have repeatedly opposed the legions of Thay in battle, the more violent nature of the Foehammer's dogma was highly favored in the city.[31]
  • Temple of Umberlee: One of the largest temples of Umberlee in all of Faerûn renown for sending thugs to pillage ships in port in order to collect offerings for their goddess.[22]
  • Temple of Waukeen: A temple to Waukeen, who was popular with the middle class.[35]
In addition to these prominent churches, the city had many smaller temples dedicated to lesser powers, such as Auril and Malar, unpopular deities like Gond[7] or the God-Kings of Mulhorand,[36] or those whose perspectives were out of alignment with the Red Wizards, such as Helm, Ilmater, Lliira, Oghma and Tyr. There was even an old temple of Myrkul that boasted a single priest, and a hidden subterranean temple of Mystra that operated in relative safety from the city's ruling wizards.[7]
